notes: kb/Work PB5130 (landed). §1989:A.2.12.3 AR1: "a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600", no upper limit. At --std 85 CobolDate.DateOfInteger takes any positive day count (DialectBehavior.IntegerDateFormBounded inactive): DATE-OF-INTEGER (3067672) is 100000101, and DISPLAY of the function shows all nine digits (FunctionValueField.OfDigits). A count whose YYYYMMDD the 64-bit result cannot hold is the incorrect-argument default 0. Witnesses 1989-AR-A_2_12_3-1 and pb5130_integer_date_year_10000_85.

next.reason: 1989: argument-1 'is a positive integer that represents a number of days succeeding December 31, 1600', with no upper bound. 2023 §2023:15.22.3 AR1 requires 'a value in integer date form', which §2023:15.5.2 defines with the same meaning but adds 'shall be less than or equal to the value of FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DATE (99991231), which is 3,067,671'. An argument above 3,067,671, in range in 1989, is now out of range (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION per §2023:15.3 AR14). Stricter. §2023:15.5.2 has no catalog row.
